review_title: Rugged Unlocked Smartphone for GSM Cellular Networks
review_text:
This CAT S31 RUGGED WATERPROOF SMARTPHONE (Unlocked) is my first unlocked phone, and I really didn’t know what to expect. What I discovered is that there are two types of phones: (1) phones intended for GSM networks (AT&T, T-Mobile, Cricket, and other carriers), and (2) phones intended for CDMA networks (mainly Verizon and Sprint).

If you try to sign this GSM phone up for a cellular plan at Verizon or Sprint—using the “Bring Your Own Phone” option—you are asked to check the phone’s compatibility by entering the 15-digit IMEI number (conveniently printed on the outside of the CAT S31 box). Both networks return “incompatible”, so you will need to Google GSM to find compatible networks. (You can’t add this incompatible phone to an existing Sprint or Verizon plan, either.)

Cricket responded “compatible” and offered to sell me a SIM card and plan; ATT said “compatible, but can’t locate a suitable SIM card”, so I stopped there and went with Cricket. There seem to be quite a few GSM networks around, though.

By law, the phone will make emergency calls without a SIM card connection to a cellular network.

While waiting for a SIM card and cellular connection, I can use this phone to connect to the Internet through my home network (powered by Comcast Xfinity). Once connected to the network, my phone syncs automatically with my Google account. The phone is generally quite easy to set up—especially if you’re already familiar with the Android interface and navigation.

This is an extremely rugged phone, as advertised. It has a thick rubber backing, sloped corners, and thick rubber bumpers on the edges. There are rubber-stoppered openings in the bumpers for a USB charging cable, SIM card insertion, and Micro SD card insertion. With the stoppers closed, the phone is highly resistant to dust, damp, and short immersions in water. Picking up the phone, it feels so sturdy, I feel no need to purchase any additional case or screen protector. The phone is comfortable to hold.

The phone has front- and rear-facing cameras. The cameras don’t match the quality of my Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge phone, but they’re perfectly adequate for a heavy-duty outdoor-workplace-use phone. The navigation isn’t as slick as the fancier phone, either, as the phone has physical buttons to push for “home”, “back”, and “recent apps” (instead of icons on the touchscreen).

review_title: After three weeks, it's even better
review_text:
I deleted the first review that I posted on the day after receiving this phone. It was a good review but it turns out that this phone is even better than I first thought.

I replaced my Huawei Mate SE with this product. The Mate SE is a great phone but I needed a bit more RAM. When I saw the Honor View 10 with 6 GB and 128 GB of storage, I ordered it. I assumed it would be a Mate SE with a bit more kick. Turns out that this phone is way, WAY more :

It charges fast. The battery life is incredible. The screen display, colors and resolution are phenomenal. Performance is FAST. The sound quality is a delight to hear. The Music and Video apps bundled with the phone aren't the greatest, but I use VLC and am very happy. How the heck did they get such wondrous and full sound to come out of those itty bitty speakers??? Watching a movie is great!!! I'm not a photographer, but I'm very happy with the photos it takes. This phone is a b@llbuster!

By the way, I tried both the Galaxy S9+ and the Huawei Mate 10 Pro. Wound up returning them both. They were okay, but they weren't that great, especially not in their respective price tags great. Unlike the Mate SE where the fingerprint sensor was away from the camera lenses, the S9+ and Mate 10 Pro had it right underneath the lenses. Fumble to touch the sensor and you smear the lenses. Not just dumb but moronic. The Honor View 10's fingerprint sensor is under the screen. Perfect! Now I can use my thumbs.

This phone is just plain wonderful. Remember when you were a kid (I'm 60) and got that one toy at Christmas which you played with for more than a day, went back to that same toy over and over again and never got bored with it? This phone is that toy. Enjoy!!!

A couple other things. I use this with Tracfone. Absolutely no problems. When I removed the Tracfone SIM from the Mate SE and installed it into this unit, I was instantly up and running. A great free app you can get from the Play Store is Network Cell Info Lite which will give you detailed information on your cell, wifi, signal, speed, etc. Seeing a map to your serving tower is really neat, too.
I LOVE this phone!!!!!

review_title: Making and receiving calls, and much more
review_text:
Basically, what I need in a cell phone is the ability to make calls to people I want to speak with, and to receive calls from people who need to speak with me. That's it!

Of course, any old phone will do that, but there's my image to look out for, so I also want it to look expensive and sleek, to be able to pick up signals even in office blocks, have long battery life, and have tons of cool features to talk about, even if I never use them. The ability to withstand sudden impacts and the occasional passing shower is also an asset.

So far, this phone has met all my needs as follows:

(1) It makes calls just great
(2) It receives calls clearly
(3) It looks trendy with its cute little handle-shaped antenna, which is very useful as a handle when pulling it from your bag
(4) It's not the most expensive, but it looks like a million bucks
(5) It picks up signals in office buildings (and elsewhere)
(6) Excellent battery life
(7) It fell and survived (JAN 16 - EDIT: IT FELL AGAIN AND THE INTERIOR DISPLAY IS DAMAGED. THE PHONE HOWEVER STILL WORKS)
(8) It got drizzled on and survived

Feature wise:

(1) It has a camera and can take video recordings
(2) You can set up speed dialing fairly easily
(3) It has flashing lights when it rings, and you can change the light shows (or turn the darn thing off already)
(4) Lots of memory for lots of numbers, e-mail addresses, birthdays and so on
(5) You can set different lights and ring tones for each one of your friends
(6) You can show a different photo on the display outside to the one inside.
(7) It has a stopwatch and calculator
(8) It has a loud speaker! (All the better for us all to hear you my dear)
(9) Media player, and use can use a headphone (sold separately)
(10) Voice activated commands (Answer and Busy, or you choose)
(11) Changeable covers to meet your mood (Always gray, thank you)
(12) Big numbers and letters for easy dialing and text messages (if you're the texting kind)
(13) It can vibrate!!!!!!!! (Call me back! Call me back!)
(14) I had somebody send me Crazy Frog as a ring tone, so I can REALLY annoy my favorite people. (It's got Bluetooth and infra-red for transferring data - but don't ask me how to use them - I just like saying that I have it)
(15) Lots of shortcut keys to get to things quickly
(16) Internet services (I can't use these yet, because my provider doesn't offer it)
(17) it has a very nice alarm clock feature

Things not so great about it:

(1) The position of the camera button is bad for me. I use a Body Glove case, and when I pull out the phone, I sometimes inadvertently take a picture on the way out. Similarly when trying to open it in a hurry.
(2) The picture quality isn't the best
(3) It's not easy to open with one hand
(4) While the volume buttons are conveniently placed on the side, I sometimes hit them when answering a call.
(5) The sound is kinda tinny
(6) Not enough cool ring tones (yeah, I can get more, but using Bluetooth means I have to read the manual)
(7) You have to remember to use the arrow keys to get to other tabs in the menus to see all the features
(8) Speed dialing needs two buttons (I'm accustomed to holding down one button)
(9) The lights go out really quickly before you can finish deciding what you're looking for

Overall, a great phone for the price, and it looks good too.

Amanda Richards, January 10, 2006

review_title: The biggest problem is Straight Talk!
review_text:
My husband got this phone a few months ago.
It works fine as a phone, WHEN Straight talk is working.

You can take photos, send texts easily, and overall, everything works okay.
The texting area is a little small for my husband, who has to use a pen to
poke the little letters because of his big fingers.
Calls are clear, we haven't had any drop yet, so that gets a thumbs up as well.

BUT....

He uses the "All You Need" plan with this phone, which gives you 30 days of service,
with 1000 minutes of talk and 1000 texts, as well as some odd amount of web time.
That's all well and good, and it works well for him.
However, the Straight Talk Reserve plan has huge flaws for the All You Need cards.

Every single month, it is a nightmare. We add a card to the reserve a few days before the
30 days is up. Each and every time so far, the phone stops DEAD on the 30th day, and the reserve
does not automatically roll over. Each time, we have to call tech support (a long, long wait
to reach someone who does not speak English as their native language) and go through the arduous
process of resetting the minutes and having him text *2_ _ _ _ (some number, not sure what it is)
to reactive the phone.

That part is beyond ridiculous.
It is annoying, time wasting, and very inconvenient when you use your phone for work.

At this point, we are ready to change. Both of my college aged kids use Straight Talk
on the Unlimited Everything plan and don't have this problem. Apparently, the inconvenience is
limited to the All You Need, perhaps in some twisted attempt to get to you upgrade to the more
expensive plan. Either that, or they have really bad programming on the reserve!

Either way, it is bad enough that my husband is ready to move on to another phone and another provider.
It's a shame, since the calls are clear.
But you have to be able to count on your phone, and you just can't with this one (which is for Straight Talk).

UPDATE:
As of May 2013, after yet another bad experience in April with the All You Need plan not working correctly,
We ordered another phone from another company, and have changed over to Net10. It isn't perfect either, but the
unused minutes roll over without expiration dates, and no hassles at all about loading extra time.
Buh-bye Straight Talk! You really need to work on your service! It chased us away.

I'm no stranger to Nuu handsets, I have owned and reviewed others including a Nuu X6 that I left a favorable review for back in 2019/2020. My kid even used it as a daily driver for over a year back then.
It was a good value at the time, not great hardware but you got a lot for your money. Back then, low end handsets were still available with 2GB of ram, so for the money you got a pretty decent display paired with 3GB of RAM and Android 9. It also came with 3 months of prepaid Mint Mobile service in the box, which made it an excellent choice as a starter phone with it's own service- perfect for your kids first handset.
Here we are 2.5 years later with an updated handset that has... well, an updated version of the Android OS (Android 11 instead of 9) and not much else. It seems like a similar price point for largely similar hardware. We still have 3 GB RAM and 32 GB storage, and a Mediatek CPU that is mediocre at best. I was hoping it would at least be a faster Mediatek chip but if anything it seems somewhat laggier, although that might just be because the system is still optimizing. Either way, not impressed with the performance so far. That was a good value a couple of years ago but the expectations and demands of mobile devices have changed. The display is bigger, I'll give it that, but it is not a higher resolution.
Honestly, it feels like the same handset with similar performance at best, but years later and asking the same money. And this time, it doesn't come with the 3 prepaid months so I can't even say it is as good of a value. Apps demand more resources these days, the newer OS is more optimized for devices with more RAM, and these days even cheap phones can be found with 5G. It just feels like a hard sell now.
It's not a BAD device, it get the job done as an unlocked basic phone. But the value feels weak, I was expecting something that felt in 2022 like the X6 did in 2019. Underwhelmed.

review_title: I love the size and ergonomics, but T-MOBILE ONLY
review_text:
This is a throwback to when phones were actually light and pleasant to hold and use as... well, phones. There is NO browser on here, there is not even a camera on here. It is essentially like a cordless landline phone that you can leave the house with, which also supports SMS messages.
Calls are clear, volume is good... that is, as long as you have T-mobile service. This phone might as well be locked to that carrier because it won't work with anyone else due to VoLTE restrictions. Verizon *almost* works, I get signal bars and a 4G icon, but since I can't set the APN (there are no APN settings to be found, anywhere) I can't get the LTE to connect, and therefore there is no connection for a voLTE call to be placed. That's OK, the description says it doesn't work with Verizon so that was just wishful thinking, however I have gotten other GSM phones to work and already active VZ sim card, so it SHOULD have been possible, even if unofficially. I put a Red Pocket branded Sim on T-mobile service in for testing, and it worked fine.
There are a lot of things I like about it, the size of the buttons, the comfortable feeling in your hand, I love the simplicity and response of it, and the lock button the side means no accidental button presses. BUT, there's a lot I'm disappointed by as well. I own a flip phone from this brand that my son loves (no internet to hog his attention as a communication tool), but at least it has a camera and MMS support. This, surprisingly doesn't even have a camera. It also doesn't support picture messaging (MMS), which surprises me further since that is something that should be expected. Any phone that supports calls and texts should also include MMS as part of the texts layer. If you try to send someone a gif or picture, it just won't show up. No error message, it just doesn't work. Yet the phone has a color screen and can play media like music off an SD card from the menu. This doesn't make sense to me.

For the price, it's a cute little phone that does handle calls well. If it had a basic camera, MMS support, and maybe even a simple WAP browser, I'd give this 5 stars easily for the ergonomics alone. But as it is now, I'm kind of disappointed. There isn't a target demographic I can think of for this that wouldn't at least want MMS included.

NOTE: If buying this for a senior or child and just want a cheap basic plan, I highly recommend Red Pocket's Annual plan. Make sure you get their GSM-T so it works on T-mobile, I was able to get a plan for $30 for the year as an emergency phone, well worth the investment. But I might recommend their flip phone or a different model that supports MMS instead.

[[VIDEOID:c2219b966be26a8f0df8951bdd80cd4e]] Blu has a reputation of being a decent budget brand and this handset continues that legacy. The first thing you notice is the display- surprisingly bright even in sunlight, and extremely vibrant for the price. Graphics and games are surprisngly fluid and sharp looking, it actually feels reminiscent of Motorola G series handsets. The performance is decent too:
Geekbench 5 single core: 342
Multi Core: 1200
Those test scores aren't current flagship level, but are better than, say, the Pixel 3a series and actually competitive to flagships from not too long ago. Pretty close to a Snapdragon 835 in performance, like a Galaxy S8, yet much more battery friendly.
The finger print reader is faster and more responsive than my Galaxy S10, but to be fair the S10 has the worst of the Galaxy fingerprint readers. It even comes with a case and screen protector so you are ready to go right out of the box! But the cameras... that's where the budget nature of this handset starts to show.
The camera, despite having a large looking array, really feel low budget. Low light is a non-starter, I won't even bother sharing the noisy garbage that comes out of it. But even in good light, colors are washed out and there's a severe lack of dynamic range that clips highlights and shadows pretty quickly. See photo comparison of a yellow and red box taken next to an open window in my office. The Galaxy S10 and Pixel3A properly captured light from outside the window as well as some detail in the black batteries under the box. It shouldn't be a surprise that those pictures look similar straight out of the camera app, the Pixel and Galaxy S series have some of the best "standard by which others are judged" camera performance in the industry. The Blu phone, however, overexposed the window, lost all detail in the battery, and the colors just overall look bad compared to them. I also took a picture trying the "depth mode" of a keychain on my wood colored desk, and the bokeh effect is a mess. It doesn't make any sense, blurring out random parts of the wood grain pattern and not looking like real bokeh AT ALL.

Basically, this is a decent phone with decent performance and a very nice sized and vivid display for the money! But if cameras are any kind of priority to you, look elsewhere.

[[VIDEOID:ce99f90067d0e66fd0c7e3d808e0217]] I think it is kind of bizarre that they are marketing this as as phone for elderly and children. Its more like a classic throwback to the durable basic phones of yesteryear, but underneath the unsuspecting exterior is the heart of an Android smartphone. Essentially, this is a phone for use in an industrial setting. Like a factory floor, or other noisy/messy/loud environment that would otherwise be somewhat not friendly to smartphones. There is no play store, and the UI is heavily customized to work with the form factor, but some apps can be sideloaded if you know how Android works.
This is NOT a smartphone replacement, but rather a durable work phone for those who want to take some of the conveniences of a smartphone without the smartphone. See the attached video for a longer explanation and to see it in action.

review_title: AWESOME PHONE FROM A GREAT SELLER
review_text: Was really skeptical about buying a renewed phone yet alone the Samsung S20+ because I didn't know what condition it was going to be. But to my surprise, the phone works great, NOT A SCRATCH!!! Battery life is good, fingerprint works fine and had no issues with the phone. This seller really did their job.

Apparently a few steps shy of a basic smartphone, and exactly what I need. I've even emailed a few photos successfully! I am still getting acquainted, but the touch screen is wonderful -- it is sensitive, so you have to learn your touch. I can now make fast movements without hitting the wrong buttons accidentally. It didn't take me long to learn basic texting, dialing, receiving calls, retrieving messages, straight-ahead photography (nothing fancy). I am enjoying my phone after just a month, without even teaching myself all it has to offer.

A great bonus is the LG840G is wired for WiFi use! You will not be charged precious minutes for talk time. I have to check this out, but a friend told me to be careful, that instead, you may be charged data/data storage fees. If I find this is so, I will come back and amend this review.

Anther bonus, I think, is that when I finally expand my life to really need smartphone bells and whistles, I believe this phone will have stepped me up nicely into that arena. As it is, this phone has more than enough to fill my current music-listening, audio- and video-recording, scheduling, note-taking, social networking, web-based needs. This is a only 2.0 MP camera, but I was recently complimented on a photo I took (and texted on the spot!).

It's a great design -- looks like smartphones in my circle of friends, so there was a LOT more respect toward me and my phone than previously. In fact, 3 people on separate occasions thought I had finally gotten a smartphone, and only me and Tracfone know for sure...

I've only had it a month and I'm a slow learner, so I'm sure there is much more to get to know, but I am loving this phone as is.

review_title: IF THIS CAN MAKE IT THROUGH MY HUSBAND IT CAN MAKE IT THROUGH ANYTHING
review_text:
(WARNING- This is an in depth review designed to help anyone interested in making a sincere buying decision. If you prefer a short summary, see section marked THE BOTTOM LINE near the end of the review.)

When it comes to phones, well, electronic devices in general, if it is going to break or malfunction, my husband will bring it out of them. He is a contractor and runs his own business, so having a phone that works and is tough without interruption of malfunction or frustration is a MUST. I waited an extra long time after getting this phone to have him use it just to see how it would stand up. Let's see how this phone worked out for him.

WHAT PHONE WAS HE USED TO USING?
The phone that he used previously was a Motorola Moto G3 with Android updated to the most current level equal to this phone at the time that he started using this phone instead.

WHAT IS THIS PHONE LIKE?
First thing I had a hard time convincing him of was that he could not get a case for this phone. It is built so that it does not need a case, the phone itself is sealed and put into a strong case with strong screen. I am going to break down the features into different sections labeled so you can find out what you want to know more easily:

INSTRUCTION BOOK
Very well laid out, this instruction book makes the phone very easy to learn even for someone who has no experience with cell phones before. It also has a good layout so that someone who is familiar with cell phones can find what they need to know quickly and easily.

BACK CASE
This is a strong back case on this phone. It is meant for heavy duty use and claims to be water resistant/proof. I never say anything is truly water resistant, but that is what is on the literature.

FRONT GLASS
Not at all fragile looking, this works well and is very sensitive- he had to turn down the sensitivity a bit.

VOLUME UP/DOWN
The right side of the phone as you look at it has the volume up button on top and a SEPARATE BUTTON for volume down. This makes it easy in one respect because you are not mistakenly pushing it the wrong way. On the other hand, there are two buttons on each side which in a hurry is easy to mistake which side you are supposed to use and results in turning the phone into a sleeping/soft off position.

POWER and PROGRAMMABLE
The two buttons on the opposite (left) side as you look at the front of the phone are the on and off button and the programmable button.

PROGRAMMABLE BUTTON
This is a really cool feature. You can set the programmable button to manage incoming calls, do a Google search, or use the flashlight. You can also use the PTT (push to talk) service with this button if you so choose.

SIM CARD
There is capacity for two sim cards- a regular and nano sim. They will both work, but only one will support 3g/4g service. The other will support 3G only. There is a waterproof "cap" that presses into place over this area to protect it from water damage if it is in properly.

MICRO SD CARD
This card goes into a slot and locks in with a waterproof door covering it if you are sure it is in tightly. You can use up to 128MB size Micro SD card.

FUNCTION BUTTONS
This is one of his favorite features- they are actual BUTTONS. No more pressing the screen for his functions. They are solid well built buttons that are easy to press and use.

TRANSFER OF INFORMATION FROM OLD TO NEW PHONE
This was such an easy task it was almost unbelievable. Information transferred quickly and perfectly. We were impressed at how well the set up of the phone went.

CALLS
Calls are easy to do. The call quality is excellent and the performance is as good (or better) at times as the Moto G3 which was a solid performing phone that gave the best performance of any phone we have ever used, including the "high end" phones.

VOLUME
The volume of the phone is good. Speaker phone is not always as loud on the other callers end, but on the end of the user, it is good. It is still possible to hear in a rather noisy van, but challenging. Ear phone or wireless speaker would be a better choice if you plan to use this regularly in a truck or van.

MUSIC
My husband uses his phone a lot for music- either from the Micro SD card or from FM radio. Reception is great and he is very surprised at how well this phone plays music from either radio or Micro SD. I have to say that I thought he was using a speaker the other day. When I saw it was just his phone, I really was impressed!

INTERNET PERFORMANCE
This works a bit nicer than his previous phone when it comes to internet usage. When having to use GPS, internet search, or find other information, this phone performs very well.

SCREEN VIEW
This screen is amazing. Crystal clear, beautiful color, and excellent definition make this phone a pleasure to use. I take his phone now and then to make a call because it is such a pleasure to use and view the screen.

DURABILITY
This is a solid phone. Honestly, it is one of the most rugged phones I have used, including the Rugby which was the most rugged we have used previous to this. The performance is great, the visual is wonderful, and the size is not cumbersome or too dainty either. I would say that if dropped in water, or left out in the rain (which has happened to this phone) will not damage the phone as long as it is not a severe abusive situation. (Like shooting it from a missle launch into the ocean, maybe? HAHA)

SENSITIVITY
This phone has a glove mode. That means that you can set it to be more sensitive on those days you have to work with gloves on. This feature works great although at times, he sets it and forgets it and tends to mute everyone he is talking to until he sets it back again (by just putting the phone up to his face- it mutes people)

BATTERY
With constant daily use, my husband only has to recharge this like every five or six days depending on how heavily he is using it for music and other tasks. It charges pretty quickly too.

ANY CAVEATS?
My husband has a tendency to do and undo things and have no idea how he did it. He is all about doing the jobs and getting them done, but when it comes to phones and computers, well, he is a bit of a Magoo at times. Other times he is a real pro. I guess it depends on whether his mind is on a job he is doing or if he can put more brain power into thinking about his phone. Yes, he has erased his fish pond wallpaper, muted people he is talking to, and managed to dial someone by mistake multiple times, but other than that, this phone has the best record of NOT allowing him to make mistakes of any I have seen so far.

HOW LONG HAS HE BEEN USING THIS PHONE?
I think we have had this about five or six months now, so he has been putting it through a lot in that amount of time. It is still in wonderful shape and performing beautifully at the time of this review.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Waterproof (if sealed properly) with extra features for contractors, this phone is one tough phone. It has held up beautifully for five or six months now, has excellent visual clarity and solid performance and is PERFECT for my contractor husband who is VERY rough on phones.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS for this one. I am very impressed at how well it has held up, but also how fool proof it has been for my husband who is notoriously rough on phones.

review_title: Beautiful phone. Too bad it crashes if you install apps. Yes, I'm talking about "Unfortunately My Launcher Has Stopped Working"
review_text:
Gorgeous phone, nice specs, if only it worked. Seriously, My Launcher crashes--you know the thing that runs the home screen. Kinda basic requirement to have a functional launcher. All manner of apps crash. I mean, I should say, if you don't install any apps, it works fine. If you want to install apps on this phone--and you do, that's why you got a phone with 64GB of storage--then it kinda sucks as a phone capable of running basic apps like news, weather, and clock.

I called Blu. They were open, and it didn't take long for me to get a human being. But they told me to do basic stuff I'd already done--like I've done factory reinstalls and done all the stuff the internet suggests. So they had me email them screenshots with info about my phone, of error messages, and info about the apps that were crashing. After 20 screenshots, I'd had enough screenshotting stuff going wrong.

You know what? THEY SENT ME INSTRUCTIONS ON HOW TO RESET THE BLU LIFE ONE X2. Not the MINI. I mean, sure, I can do another hard reset, but I don't imagine it's going to make a difference coz I've already done plenty of hard resets.

BLU, get it together.

I paid a few bucks more to purchase from Chubbiestech based on a review and to avoid any problems. (Reading about the A10 reviews was scaring me until I realized I was reading the wrong product lol.) This is for the Samsung Galaxy S10e. Being from the S- product line, it's Samsung's flagship product and you can read the history and differences between the models on Wikipedia. I found this information very helpful.

I lucked out with the right Seller and got a phone that really seems brand new and works excellent in every way. (A previous purchase of a different model and seller was excellent in every way but then we discovered it wouldn't charge.) I'm so happy I bought this!

Pros

Mine was in new condition without a scratch, and functions perfectly in every way. I was able to load SmartSwitch on my old J7 and only had to manually download a matching icon set (and create a new Samsung account to download it.) Everything else (including my custom wallpaper from an outside source) transferred exactly.

I wanted a smaller profile/screen because I really loved my J7 and can easily operate it with one hard. I find modern phones too large and heavy and I'm not a gamer. The S10e's profile is surprisingly *smaller* than the J- series and fit my desire. Could easily fit inside a shirt pocket.

It runs way faster than my old phone and I verified with DevCheck that it does indeed have 6 Gigs of Ram. That's more than I ever had before and so it seems real speedy and capable to me and also 128 Gigs of space is way more than I ever thought of using.

I mostly only use my phone as a music source and the sound quality thru my headphones is superb, like my J7 which I prefer to the modern soundboards that I have to tweak; I don't have to use the equalizer on this and the bass is great.

The Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, screentouch and call quality (and charging) all work great. The mobile data connection on my old sim for some reason is much faster (30M??) on 4GLTE and the upload speed is 3x my old phone too, I can't imagine why. But the connection with the same service is just stronger and has much better coverage. I didn't realize it was the old phone limiting it. That's like broadband over 4G lol.

I simply slipped in my old Sim and it connected with no problem or troubleshooting.

Anyway the S- series hardware of this phone is superb. Mine came with Android 12 which I understand is the highest available for this model. My J7 was stuck in Android 8. I didn't want to upgrade to a phablet nor pay a lot for features I didn't want to begin with.

Caveats/Tips

I never used a case before but this phone is so small (yay!) AND slippery I needed to buy a case. Don't want to drop it and scratch the screen because my big clumsy fingers can't hold onto it. I don't have a problem navigating the screensize.

Had to manually customize icons after installing everything. This requires a Samsung account. (You can delete it from Accounts afterward if you wish.)

If you use Smart Switch to transfer and duplicate your experience from your old phone you need to unpair the devices listed under Bluetooth and re-pair them for them to work on your new phone.

Many/Most of your programs transferred and websites will require you to log-in again (so you'll need your passwords) but the data (pics/docs/program files) transferred without a hitch. (You can download Smart Switch on your old phone from Google Play.)

My phone has the annoying T-mobile start-up screen (less annoying if you turn the sound off) but it doesn't harm anything functionally.

Samsung apps preinstalled cannot be uninstalled or disabled. However Google apps can be.

The battery is small (3100) but I'm used to that from the J7. I tried a larger capacity battery in my J7 but became impatient with the charging time so actually prefer the quick charging of these.

This review is obviously for folks who may not have done this before or are doubtful about the quality of the renewed product.

I'm totally happy with the new phone and the process of setting it up was seamless. Definitely worth it and you saved a lot of money! (Now you can peruse the internet and modern apps like the Joneses! :)

Update: It's a bit too small to be honest, and very SLIPPERY, however still prefer this to the large ones. Wish they still made J-size. But everything works great, sounds great and I'm getting 50M download on LTE! All I do is listen to music so it's fine for my needs. Great price for a fast phone.

review_title: very good phone for the price, Samsung bloatware is easier to deal with than in past years
review_text:
Now that the price on this phone has gone down to $600, it is a very good deal for the price.

The Snapdragon 865 processor is more than fast enough for anything I want to do. 6GB of memory is less than some other phones in this price range, but it is still more than enough for most people.

The phone feels very solid despite the plastic back. If you use any kind of case, you won't even notice the plastic back.

The phone supports 25W fast charging, but for some reason they only included a 15W charger in the box. Buying the 25W charger separately is a waste of money as well as a waste of the natural resources that were used on the 15W charger. Amazon sells decent 25W fast chargers for less than $15, so cheaping out on the charger is a real lame move by Samsung. You can search Amazon for 15W chargers that support "USB-C PPS" mode and are UL Certified.

The screen looks beautiful when you turn on the 120Hz mode. This does burn your battery more quickly, but the battery is big enough that it still lasts all day.

The screen has been very responsive to me. I have read bug reports about screen glitches for some people. Samsung has already released bug fixes that hopefully have fixed this. I advise only buying this phone from an authorized dealer with no hassle returns so you don't have to worry about this bug.

The phone does have a lot of Samsung bloatware. I owned a Samsung S-series phone several years ago and the bloatware was really bad then. This one is much better. You don't even need to create a Samsung account to use the phone now. Most of the Samsung bloatware (other than the camera app) won't work if you don't have a Samsung account, but if you never use it, this isn't a problem. There are several tutorials online about disabling all the bloatware if you never want to see any of it on your screen.

The triple camera setup on this phone is very good for this price level. The telephone camera works great up to 3X in good light. Image quality deteriorates quickly if you zoom in past 3X or in lower lighting conditions. Telephoto cameras are getting rare in this smartphone price range, so I'm glad this phone has one. I really like using the telephoto lens for landscape and nature photography. The normal and wide angle cameras work better in lower light situations (including indoor situations), though not as good as the iphone or Google Pixel phones. Pictures do tend look more processed than with some other phone cameras. Some people like the Samsung look. Other people prefer more natural looking photos. You should try to look at sample photos before buying the phone, since you cannot completely disable the Samsung photo processing.

This phone comes with Android version 10 out of the box, which is one version behind the Android version 11 that the Google Pixel phones are shipping with. Samsung promises software support with 3 version updates, but that is a little misleading since 1 of those version updates will be just to catch up with the current Android version 11. Still, 3 years of bug fixes and security patches is better than what Samsung used to offer.

Pros:

Cons:
The keys stick - badly. Say, if you push the '1' key - it will just stay down. This makes entering phone numbers difficult. Texting basically impossible. I returned the phone once due to this issue. I got a new one. It worked for awhile, but now is experiencing the same issues. And, just as some keys stick in the down position, some won't push at all. Also, sometimes the wrong key will enter. For example: even when I'm extremely careful to push the '*' key, '9' will be entered instead. It is very difficult for me to call into teleconferences due to how hard it is just to get the '*' key to depress in a timely manner.

My screen on the phone I returned also got stuck 'on' for awhile. I attribute it to the stuck keys as well. I was very reluctant to buy a non-flip phone. The problems I've had with this one are making me promise myself when this contract is up, that I will switch back.

It's very difficult to get the USB port flap open.

The wired headset that comes with the phone apparently distorts my voice quite a bit - at least according to my co-workers. So, it's hard to make hands free calls. I haven't tried another.

Software wasn't really thought through:
Stored contacts display phone numbers in tiny, tiny, tiny font. The screen is HUGE - it would be nice if I could use a bit of it to display the numbers larger.

Often, phone numbers are displayed without hyphens in the logical locations - it would be nice if they had built this into the software. (i.e., 1234567890 vs. 123-456-7890)

Font choices are limited - none that easy to read.

No options for displaying larger fonts.

This is my first "wallet friendly" phone and I have to say I am extremely impressed with the overall package. There is a ton of storage, a capable chipset, great cameras, and absolutely zero software bloat. It's snappy and rugged....battery life is phenomenal.

Pros:
RUGGED - This beast has a full metal body with rubber bumpers on the corners. SIM/SD slot and charging ports are sealed. I've dropped it several times to test it out and it has survived drops of four feet onto tile and cement with no issue. I have no doubt this thing can withstand some water, too. It's crazy.
BATTERY - Battery life is amazing. With my normal daily usage I get down to about 84% by the end of the day. That's some light gaming, reading news, browsing the internet, a few calls, and thirty-ish texts. Maybe a few YouTube videos thrown in the mix as well. I am genuinely impressed. Beats the pants off my old Samsung S10+.
CAMERAS - Macro camera is great. Wide angle is decent...Normal 64MP is loaded with detail. Now because it's not using software filters to render the image it isn't exactly the most accurate photo, but it still looks great. I will be using this for videos, for sure. Auto-focus is quick and it just takes great video all around. The selfie camera says 32MP, but it isn't the best. Images are passable, and you get some nice effects in low-light. I'll probably stick with the rear cameras.
CHIPSET/RAM - I'm not a professional who knows a lot about capabilities and specs, but I can proudly proclaim that this has enough horsepower under the hood to play Asphalt 9 and Genshin Impact without noticeable frame droppage. Asphalt 9 at highest settings runs like a dream. Default on Genshin was delivering a smooth experience.
128GB - Has plenty of storage built in for all my apps. Right now I've got 432 GAMES installed and about 20 random must-have apps. Really putting it through its paces to see if I like it...Plus, you can toss in a microSD card for more room for videos and pictures. I've got a 200GB card in now and it works fine.
CALL QUALITY - Sounds just like any phone I've ever used....No complaints.
BLOATWARE - There is nothing pre-installed other than a few essential Google Apps. Very clean Android 11 experience right out of the box. I installed a custom launcher so I could do my own thing, but it's overall a perfect beginning setup.

Cons:
CHARGING - It's slow. It's like...really slow. Takes about an hour to go from 80% to 100%.
SOUND - Not very loud, and a little tinny. I've been pampered by LG phones in the past with great sound. This is obviously one of the corners they cut to reach this price.
CAMERA - I know I had good things to say about the cameras, but I also have some bad things. By default stabilization is off and navigating the app is...weird. Also, in low light the camera performance is sub-par. In good lighting, though, I can get some great photos. Doesn't compare to an iPhone 13 Pro Max or LG V60...but absolutely better (to me) than the Samsung S10+.

For a budget device, this has actually become my daily phone. I use an iPhone for work, but this little Cubot is my new personal device. It's highly comparable to all the other phones I've used...I honestly can't see much difference with this screen and the screen on higher end devices...So for me, this is just a nice solid hunk of phone. Watched a lot of reviews before deciding on this one. Glad I got it.

review_title: Best TracFone ever - which isn't saying much
review_text: If you use TracFone, then you are a cheapskate.  Welcome to the late 20th century, cheapskate.  This unit looks like a smartphone, but it isn't.  But it is the smartest dumb phone ever offered by TracFone.  You should buy it, if only for the triple minutes for the life of the phone.  At $35, this phone will pay for itself at 7 cents per minute instead of the 10 cents per minute which is the best airtime rate previously available on TracFone, which required a "double minutes" phone.  The LG840g sports a music player which plays mp3 and m4a (AAC) file formats, you can check your email (rudimentary graphics) & send emails.  Hook up to WiFi to use the browser (rudimentary) and email functions for free, but note:  YOU CANNOT USE VOIP TO MAKE FREE PHONE CALLS using the WiFi.  This fone may be slightly dumber than it looks, but TracFone isn't!  The memory upgrades to 32 GB with a micro-SD card.

review_title: Smart DumbPhone also plays mp3 and iTunes AAC music files
review_text: I have been a TracFone user for several years, because you can actually get service for $60 per YEAR (yes, that's $5.00 per month) plus 10 cents per minute if you use a double-minutes phone.  This model is the first I have owned which gives triple minutes, which will lower the price of airtime to 7 cents per minute and help pay for the phone over time.  I connect all 3 of my TracFones to a single Google-Voice phone number (the other two are basic flip-phone models sold for about $10).  I give out the Google-Voice number and all 3 TracFones ring when anyone calls it.  That way I can use Google-Voice's free services, like free voicemail and voicemail transcription to email, as well as selective blocking of unwanted calls, recording of incoming phone calls (hello, NSA!) and allowing me to save high-quality mp3 recordings of all my voicemail messages (see you in court!).  The LG-840G has a nice mp3 player (which also plays m4a AAC-encoded files from the iTunes store) plus BlueTooth capability built in, so you can go for a stroll while listening to a 32 GB micro-SD chip, and any incoming phone calls will be automatically routed to my BlueTooth open-air headphones.  When the call ends, the music resumes automatically.  I can check my Gmail on this phone (despite having 2-step verification) using 3G when outside or for free at home or anywhere there is WiFi.  The BlueTooth file transfer software allows free transfer of photos from the phone to the computer, eliminating the need to email photos that limited earlier TracFones.  This is easily the best TracFone that this cheapskate has ever owned, even if it is just a smart dumbphone.

review_title: Wonderful phone at any price, and the price overshadows modest flaws
review_text:
This is a $130 unlocked phone, and it's damn good. While it lacks compared to $400 ones (not to mention $800+ ones), it's definitely 5 stars in light of the price.

It's basically a LG 6+ (albeit with limited storage before adding a micro SD card). That's generally a good thing, though I've had mixed luck with LG phones (endless boot loops tend to sour ones faith). The screen (as well as most specs) is exceptional for the price, and while the UI imperfect, it's not a deal breaker (I tend to use a 3rd party launcher). The camera is the real Achilles heel, but the rest of the phone is the rest of Achilles! Note the older processor and Amazon ads haven't been an issue at all.

The main flaw I find in day to day use is wifi dropping. I'm optimistic of a fix, and it would be a bigger deal for a bigger price. I've used this thus far on Sprint and plan on using it on Tmobile (just move to an area with horrible Verizon coverage, so this is a great way to try other carriers without a contract).

Expandable storage, multi-carrier compatibility, tremendous batter life, and great price make it a wonderful phone. Glitchy wifi and a mediocre (by 2018 standards--still pretty good compared to 3-4 year old flagship phones that sell for as much or more used) camera don't hold this back at all.

This is an amazing phone. Battery lasts a full day even with heavy gameplay. Camera is better than on i-phone 11 -- I tested it side-by-side with my girlfriend's  i-phone. She now wants to use my phone whenever taking pictures. My previous phone was BLU G9 PRO -- also a good phone, but the camera was miles behind this one. The only downside of this phone is that charging is fairly slow even with rapid-charging, however, it is not a problem with battery life. I also noticed that wireless charging is a bit sensitive and you have to pay attention that you place the phone properly on the wireless charger, you can't just slap it on there or it might not make a connection.

This phone/pda has real problems.  I too am waiting for Joe Schmoe's phone to be refurbished by Cingular and sent to me.  I am just hoping that I am within the warrantee -- something that Cingular cannot confirm, although I have had the various phones almost a year -- or just over a year.  You are asking for it if you buy this device!

As for the ads...... They live on the second screen where you stash all of your important shortcuts. They are at the top of that screen. Even so you can put one dozen shortcuts at the bottom.

Transferring was a bit of a snafu. The old phone died and the new one had no signal. It took 2.5 hours with customer service to straighten it out. They stuck with me and did not wander off. (Believe it or not!). What I think the ultimate problem was...was that after the xfer I should have cut the old phone OFF. I believe that having both phones on caused some kind of mystery problem with Verizon. As soon as I cut the old one off the transfer went through lickety split. Keep this in mind and you'll be fine. It's not in the Tracphone customer service manual so you'll need to do that yourself if you have a problem. Help thyself.

Also, you'll need to set up voicemail again. And if you're smart you will grab a copy of Airdroid. With a copy on your phone and one on your computer you can use your computer to do all sorts of neat file things on your phone like transferring custom ringtones and such. A hint: Your custom message mp3 or Ogg goes into the "notification" folder. You'll find it.

I see NO reason to spend $800-$1000 for a big brand when you can get the same pleasure for under $200 bucks. Keep in mind though that Tracphone is phasing out triple minutes. Do like I did with your old triple minute phone. Load it up before the switch. That way you'll get at least those triple minutes transferred.

It's a good modern phone with all the bells and whistles. And the camera is outstanding! Video is good too.

review_title: There Are Several Better Devices Available
review_text:
I just returned my T-Mobile wing after a week and a half of solid use. It had a lot of strong points but some major drawbacks ruined the deal. First, those shopping for a device like this are probably looking for a fairly quick data connection. I'm sad to say that T-mobile just isn't up to par with any other, major carrier when it comes to data speeds. It's not a trivial kinda of difference eitther. Verizon has speeds on their phones that are nearly as fast or faster than DSL. With this phone it's barely comparable to a dial-up modem. Forget about Skype, forget about streaming video. It just doesn't happen at those speeds.

From a business perspective this device is very solid. Windows Mobile 6.0 offers a few crucial changes over 5.0 but the applications are what won me over. It's nearly a fully functional desktop version of Excel in this bad boy. The version of Word is top of the line as well. Outlook functionality is stellar, and... it even browses Sharepoint sites (with some limitations).

As far as the physical device itself, I have some gripes. When using it horizontally with the keyboard slid open, the screen feels very fragile and the device feels fragile over all in your hands when using it this way. I could predict that the sliding functionality would break in the very near future.. .it didn't feel sturdy in that actiona t all.

The keyboard is virtually flat, which sucks if you are typing anything other than an extremely quick text. There is no 3.5mm audio jack, it's USB and Bluetooth only. That' sunfortunate because this thing is just about the right size to replace your iPod with, and with memory cards getting as big as they are it's not such a bad alternative. Plus the Win Media Player is very cool and very comprehensitve on this guy. It can be controlled from the home menu

The overall feel of the device is great. The case is not smooth and plasticy, it's textured and has a soft feel that would obviously show fewer nicks and dings than your standard PDA. Also, just in case you wondered, the color is not as bad as it appears online. It's a very deep, dark, bluish-purple with a metallic sheen.

I can see this device having serious merit for somebody with smaller hands since it isn't that much longer than a RAZR.

In the end I sent the device back because it's Wi-Fi module failed. Let me tell you this up front... T-Mobile, not very good at technical troubleshooting. Wouldn't recommend you even bother. I made it through 3 levels of Technical support for the guy to tell me that it must be my wireless setup, despite the fact that my friend was able to connect with his T-Mobile Dash, and the Wing wasn't able to connect to ANY wi-fi connection after the first day. That's T-mobile though, I doubt you'll have success troubleshooting with any carrier on that note. The real story here is that mine was prone to defects within 48 hours of standard use.

Overall, I'd recommend it. I'm sure they would have recalled the device by now if everybody was having the wi-fi issues so I guess that's a fairly safe bet. I wasn't able to find evidence of mass defect for wi-fi capabilities on the net.

Make sure that you are comfortable with the feel of this device when it's open and the keyboard is in use before you commit to it!

review_title: Mostly Great Phone, With One Caveat
review_text:
Note: Please check the update at the bottom of my review for explanation as to why I have lowered my rating for this phone.

If I were relying upon the description of the phone printed on this page and some of the reviews here I would be extremely confused and would most likely pass this product by. Many of the reviews here seem to be written for versions that have completely different specs than the phone I received and Amazon hasn't exactly gone out of their way to clarify. I will do my best not to add to the confusion.

First of all, if you are looking for documentation for this model it is almost impossible to find. The closest you will come to finding a manual (none comes with the phone, either) is to go to LG's support site and look for model LG US997U. This phone is basically a "special edition" of that model, the main difference being the inclusion of some unremovable Amazon apps from the operating system and personalized ads that display from Amazon when your phone goes into the sleep mode. Other than that, all of the specs seem to be the same.

So, here is what you get in regards to specifications. I have double checked these myself. The only spec that I can not absolutely verify is the screen resolution, although I do believe the specs I am listing here to be accurate.

- Screen: 5.7" QHD+ Fullvision Display, Screen Resolution 2880 x 1440 pixels, 18:9 aspect ratio
- Memory 4GB RAM, 128GB Storage, Expandable to 2TB with MicroSD card
- Software Modified version of Android 7.0, Some Amazon and Google apps unremovable
- Processor Qualcomm Snapdragon™ 821 2.35 GHz + 1.6 GHz Quad-Core Custom 64-bit Qualcomm Kryo™
- Cameras: Rear Facing 5 MP Wide-Angle Lens, Front Facing Dual 13 MP Rear Cameras

Other features: Square Camera Mode, Dolby Vision™ & HDR10 Supported, Unlocked for use with AT&T, Sprint and T-Mobile (LG claims it supports Verizon as well. I can't verify.) , Hi-Fi Quad DAC playback, IP68 Water and Dust Resistant, facial rcognition and fingerprint recognition for unlock, FM Radio (works with included earbuds), 4G LTE Connectivity, Mobile Hotspot, Rear Key with Fingerprint Sensor, Internal (non-user removable) 3,300 mAh battery with included fast charger, charger/data cable included uses USB to USB-C connectors, Bluetooth (4.0?), NFC, Android Beam, DLNA Media Server, LG Air Drive, Bluetooth wi-fi and USB tethering, Enhanced LTE, VPN Manager, GPS, AKA LG G6+ Amazon Prime Exclusive, LG US997U

Important: I have no idea what the "Amazon Prime Exclusive" label means. While there are some built-in Amazon apps and an Amazon promotional screensaver that comes on when the phone is in sleep mode, there is nothing really Amazon-specific about the phone otherwise. You do NOT have to have an account with Amazon for this phone to work, let alone a PRIME account. All Amazon specific apps can be easily disabled.

Compatibility: From what I can tell, this unlocked phone will work fine on 3G, 4G and LTE networks including both CDMA and GSM. So, they should work well with Sprint, T-Mobile and AT&T as well as all of the pre-paid vendors who use their networks (Cricket, Boost, H20, Virgin Mobile, etc). The phone is physically capable of working on Verizon's network, but from my understanding it is difficult if not impossible to get Verizon to let you use an unlocked phone on their network. It will work with pretty much any other carrier or MVNO in North America though. I have mine working on AT&T/Cricket, so I can vouch for that. This phone will ONLY accept a NANO SIM Card.

Quality: Once you realize the specs that this phone comes with and see how well it is made, you will be impressed, or at least you should. It has tons of memory included for storage, lots of expandability, more than enough RAM for most applications, a very large, bright display that is capable of HD+, water and dust resistant and build quality is exceptional. It feels heavy in your hand, but is just the right size for me to hold onto it easily.

Performance is VERY snappy with its 8 core CPU and generous amount of RAM. Compared to my old Samsung Galaxy S4 it is a speed demon. It has no problem keeping up with streaming video, gaming, multimedia playback or anything else you can throw at it. Android 7 runs extremely stable on it with no glitches or other obvious problems. Mine came with the latest firmware installed. I use the DirecTV app to stream HD video on this device and the picture is perfect with no buffering, freezing or audio/video glitches.

Value. This is an oddity, because it has been bouncing around in price between $150 and $199 throughout the last several days. Either figure is a bargain though. Just look at how much the same model is priced without the "Amazon Prime Exclusive" label. It's $600+. As long as you don't mind the small Amazon screen saver that runs while the phone is in the sleep mode, you are getting a much better phone than you are paying for with this.

Documentation: Find it online from LG's website. There is just a small pamphlet that comes with the phone that tells you how to insert a SIM card. No other meaningful documentation is included. It has several warnings about only using the included USB-C charger to recharge the phone or your warranty is voided. I'm not sure how fussy this phone is, but the included fast charger works just fine for me.

Everyday use: As long as you are familiar with the Android operating system, this phone is a joy to use. It works on just about any carrier and any wi-fi network, up to the latest wi-fi AC standard. There is a tiny bit of bloatware included from LG and Amazon, but it really is minimal and can be easily hidden. Other than that, it is by far the best phone I have ever owned. And, being unlocked, you really do own it. I have no idea if it can be rooted easily, or at all. For now though I am just having fun getting used to the speed and great feature set.

UPDATE: I am lowering my rating of this phone to four stars for the following reason: After weeks of almost flawless use, I finally stumbled on to a problem with this specific "Amazon Prime Exclusive" model that likely explains why it is priced hundreds below the almost identical LG-6+. It has to do with the "screensaver" feature in which advertisements of Amazon products are shown while your phone is not in use. At first, I found this to be a completely harmless feature that had no effect on the phone's performance. Unfortunately, I have learned that this is no longer the case. When the phone goes into this customized screen saver mode it also puts to sleep some of the phone's alarm features. If you use your phone as an alarm clock or to send you reminders of events this can cause those alarms to NOT go off until you next happen to pick up the phone and swipe past the screensaver. This leaves the phone unreliable or unusable for alarms. There is no way of disabling the screensaver that I have been able to find. The "feature" is particular to this specific model, I am guessing. Hence, the deep discount. It's design is inherently defective due to Amazon's ill-conceived tampering with the operating system. I still like the phone otherwise, but just know that if you buy it that you should never depend upon its alarm functions.

UPDATE: Previously in my review I had mentioned that I had been unable to find a case that would fit this phone. Since then I have bought an Otterbox case that fits this model perfectly. Just look for the Otterbox Defender model that is built for the LG G6. It is a perfect match for this phone and fits it like a glove. I have also used this phone with cheaper cases built for the LG G6+ and those seem to fit as well. The phone has the label G-6+ silkscreened on the back. There appears to be no difference in physical size between the LG G6 and the G6+, so cases built for either model should work.

Went for Pixel 7 Pro because they offered hope and a good trade in.

Update 2022-07-07

The messaging app is a disaster trying to use RCS with other parties that don't have reliable RCS, it does not automatically drop back to SMS/MMS, so messages sit unsent and silent until you check on them. The 21st century doesn't work as well as they seem to expect.

The latest fun is that on the charging stand and charger I have been using all along, it no longer charges. It vibrates indicating charging state, the charge indicator shows charging and it discharges over night, does not feel warm like it is burning battery. It will quick charge with a cable connected charger.

Add in the ongoing bluetooth connectivity problems and whatever else I have complained about, this phone is an annoying POS.

Every time I drop it, I hope the screen is broken so I can crapcan this inexcusable, expensive crap. Maybe if I remove the case...

If only there were a decent, unmolested Android replacement available.

Update 2022-04-14

Had it a few weeks now. The camera is good, bluetooth headset doesn't usually connect or if it does, phone does not appropriately switch audio devices. The fingerprint sensor is often annoyingly slow when it works, I am still cursing the design choice to put it in the screen rather than somewhere that would have physical identification and be easy to use. Curved screen is a pointless gimmick that interferes with viewing and I suspect it is also the cause of swipe navigation being a less than positive experience. The vibration notification seems to be variable, sometimes so subtle you can miss it, sometimes feels OK. I rely on my Fitbit for silent notifications, otherwise I often miss them. I boosted my rating to three stars, there are too many significant caveats with owning this flagship device to rate it higher IMHO.

Update: Purchased another one after returning the first. The packaging of the second unit had very nice double security seals with a printed arrow on the tear tab, the first had a cheap adhesive circle that looks like it was applied haphazardly. Fingerprint sensor has been good at identifying me so far, but it's a bit slow, you have to consciously hold finger there for a second. review_title: I have a love-hate relationship with this phone
review_text:
6/20: Where to start. Probably most important is carrier support.
I was unable to activate with AT&T or Cricket. Ended up switching to T-Mobile for $20 more/mo and inferior Coverage area. In addition, T-Mobile only supports the phone on LTE so far, tho I'm paying for 5G. So those are some big caveats you might have to consider... That's PART of the distaste.
I was able to Google-copy much of my old apps, text, calendar, alarms and contacts over.
Some apps didn't copy (tunein) and other apps copied but don't seem to work, including netguard.
As for the phone itself , I required a few hard to find features including 3.5mm headphone jack (to interface with my old car stereo which has sketchy Bluetooth) . This is an increasingly rare feature, especially on more expensive phones including the 10T and 10T pro!??? I suppose the new mantra for phones is "Pay more, get Less features" that's a Woke approach if there ever was one.
Another required feature is the infra-red blaster which amazingly is still included on many Xiaomi phones. Yay.
I also require SD card expansion, another increasingly rare feature. I did prefer my old redmi lite which allowed simultaneous use of twin SIM cards and an SD card, where this phone makes you choose one or the other, even though a 7" chassis should have significantly more interior space.
Having narrowed my options to a mere TWO existing 5G phones with these features, both being Chinese manufactured, of course, since almost all are.
Another caveat is the dueling spec descriptions regarding stereo speakers... From my observation this is a DUAL speaker phone, NOT a stereo speaker phone. You get about 15% less volume from the top speaker. And it does not appear to be stereo. However, since I often find myself covering the bottom speaker with my hand, I do find the dual speaker setup useful.
It also came in handy in a loud crowded (post-Wuhan) restaurant where we were able to position the phone between us and each able to hear the streaming audio thanks to the 2nd speaker.
Loudness of these speakers is our standard cell phone expectation, not extremely loud and of course no bass response at all.

review_title: 2 Days: A thick case & the pen are absolute necessities for this GREAT camera...phone
review_text:
OK, so I purchased this phone because of the camera. I had read so much about it and for the first time in forever I was tempted to change from my 3rd edition of the Galaxy 7 Active (I have replaced mine 3 times because I like that phone so much as it has actual buttons so there is a smaller chance of inadvertently hitting the screen and initiating an unintended action and will hold up to my actions). That phone took really good photos, but it still couldn't come close to my 35mm camera. This one does and it has options unheard of in a SLR camera.
The photos attached are a great example. If you have had puppies you know how absolutely difficult it is to get a photo because they move so much and so quickly. With this camera...er phone....it takes about 10 frames before the shutter is engaged so even if he moved, I was able to go through the frames and select the one that got him before he moved. The first photo was the beauty shot that I wouldn't have had as he moved right as I clicked the shutter. I was able to get it from reviewing the motion photo and the frames right before I clicked. Similarly without that option I wouldn't have captured photos 2 or 3 or 4 as he was in motion as I shot every single one of those photos. How many times have you said, rats he moved when taking a photo? Particularly if you are shooting animals or children you know you are just as likely to miss the great shot you see in your lens because in the second it takes you to react and shoot, they move. Whoever came up with this motion photo that captures a bunch of frames before you click is a genius.
I have started watching YouTube videos because this camera is in many ways a completely new and different way of taking photos and video. Oh and if you want to select a frame from your video and turn that into a jpeg photo, you can do so.
I am really excited to take my walks this summer. I love macro shots of flowers and bugs, as well as sky shots when a storm is coming in. I typically select the best 10 or so shots taken over the summer in my daily walks to share with others in the area. With this phone I should have even better results. I won't have to go into the neighbor's yards to get up close vegetation shots as the zoom on this is unreal.
I find I use my phone more and more as a substitute for a tablet and with this phone I can see that I may do so by choice. It may be primarily intended to make phone calls but for most the functions are so good that it may do far, far more than that.
The pen and a case with a thick edge are absolute necessities. It is so much easier to navigate the page with the pen and with the pen you don't leave fingerprints. As I am using the screen to review photos, keeping it clean is a must. I have had Samsung pens come with a Chromebook and wasn't impressed, but with this one you will need to watch a separate video on just the functionality of the pen.
A case is needed both to stop inadvertent clicks as your fingers curve around the phone holding it and to enable you to hold it more steady when shooting photos/videos. I tried it without the case and it was a bust. I have nerve damage and can't feel the ends of 5 of my fingers and have nasty arthritis on top of that. The case will also protect the phone when I drop it and I will drop it, that is a given. Holding the phone resulted in numerous inadvertent clicks around the edge. There is an app you can download to create an edge border that will not be effected by touch but I would rather keep the edges as is and grab hold of a case. (I tried the app and it did help, but I felt it took up to much of that beautiful display).
I would also recommend a screen protector. It seems like a no brainer to me as screen breakage is the number one needed repair to cell phones and even with gorilla glass if you are constantly carrying this, getting it in and out, etc. you are going to strike that screen.
Oh and the camera makes good calls as well.....I mean the phone does!
I will update later, but if you are a novice there are a ton of YouTube how to videos available to teach you how to operate this and I would recommend that you go for it, particularly if you are like me a lover of photography. With this phone Samsung has truly changed the way you can obtain high quality images as well as providing a fantastic editing program to work with after you take the shot.

review_title: Solid phone if you realize what you're getting...
review_text:
The G6 is a good phone for the price so long as you're realistic and don't try to compare it to a $900 flagship phone from another brand. For $299 (or barely more than half that when it goes on sale), you are getting a 6+ inch 1080p screen, 4 gigs of RAM, and 64 gigs of internal storage with the ability to add more via a micro SD card slot. It will work on pretty much any carrier (GSM or CDMA), the battery will get you through a work day, and while it only has one speaker, it still is pretty loud compared to many. I'll just toss a few highlight of my own in since it's already been reviewed by tons of people:

PRO: Good screen though not as bring as the G5 for comparison. 70% on this = 50% on the older G5, but still ok once you crank it up.

PRO: Cameras are not great, but good. HDR is improved over past models, detail if more than fine enough for social media and 4x6 prints. The portrait mode (background blur) could be improved but works MOST of the time.

PRO: Call reception at least in my area is good. Decent speaker and headphone jack lets you use corded headsets.

CON: Wifi can sometimes kick off and you have to re-connect it. Random and not often, but worth watching.

CON: No NFC, meaning if you want to store a credit card in it to wave over store terminals to pay for something, you're out of luck. It's turned on with the European models of this, but off on U.S. models (Booooo Moto).

CON: Moto slow with Android updates. This comes with Android 9.0 - expect maybe one major update and a few security updates over 2 years (or so) and that's it.

CON: Has a glass back but no wireless charging, so, it's fragile. Get a good case and use screen protectors.

So again - this is NOT an $800-$1,000 phone, but it comes ridiculously close to most of their features for one-third the price. I think for many people if they spent some time with this, they'd find it suits their needs just as well and could save some money. Look for sales.

review_title: Definitely not for use on T-Mobile
review_text:
BLUF: If you are using T-Mobile, or an MVNO that uses T-Mobile towers, don't buy this phone.

Pros (no particular order):
* Attractive phone, feels good in the hand
* Clear screen with reasonable -- as opposed to garish -- saturation
* Decent camera
* Great fingerprint recognition
* Easy to operate one-handed
* Snappy response
* Plenty of internal storage, plus a spot for a micro-SD card
* Dual SIM (though it's either 2 SIMS, or 1 SIM and a micro-SD card, not all three at once)
* Calls are clear... if you can actually make/receive one

Cons:
* Very poor reception
* App icons are dropped on the home screen, a la Apple, and I can't find a way to remove them (pressing and holding brings up an Uninstall option, not a Remove from screen option -- and it really does uninstall!)

I did advance research, and this phone is supposed to operate on all T-Mobile frequencies, but it has the worst reception on T-MO of any phone that I've ever owned. I get no signal at all when inside a store (Walmart, Publix, Lowes), not even enough for a text, and reception inside my house (a 40s-era frame house) is never better than 2 bars. The BLU Studio X, which cost me about half as much as this phone, is rock-solid for voice, text, and data, even in an elevator! I wanted to replace the Studio X because it's pokey and the touchscreen doesn't have the best response, but this ONE X2 Mini just doesn't cut it. The point of a smartphone is to make calls and work on the 'net; if it can't connect to do that, then it's useless. I'm returning it.

review_title: I have used the Wing for nearly 3 years, it was a decent workhorse
review_text:
Eventually, I ended up giving up using a lot of features:

1. Syncing is not reliable and you can easily erase the contents on your device.
2. As it is Windows,you can always get viruses, so using it on-line if you have sensitive data on it is a bad idea.
3. Listening to music is just about hopeless because of the proprietary jack that does not accept decent-quality earbuds that come with a jack.
4. If you take a lot of time, you can actually dumb down a movie to watch it on this device.

The speakerphone sounds distorted when the phone finds something to do, and only Microsoft knows (sometimes I wonder if they actually do) what it is. Using the headset, however, always works.

The processor is indeed slow today, and the screen resolution starts to resemble a toy. I still find that a good chess game works on it and even phone calls work at the same time (I have a 2GB memory card in it).

The 2MP camera is better than nothing but if you want to take serious photos, get a camera.

Battery life is poor, you have to charge even the new battery every day under normal use.

As opposed to many who do not have much luck with the touch screen, I use only the touch screen as it is not much slower than the keyboard but I do not have to open up the unit and I have access to special characters that the keyboard does not have. Actually, I got this phone primarily for the touch screen and there were not a too many options at the time.

You will not use Skype on this phone even on your home network (I hoped I would but it never worked). 3G, in my opinion, is an expensive toy for most, and I refuse to pay $35 a month to do what I do on my home internet connection a lot faster and a lot safer (wireless is never safe for your data).

Bluetooth is probably quite bad for you, just adds to the hefty dose of radiation your body has to put up with every day, cell phone usage added already. Never tried bluetooth but I assume it works fine.

The buttons are indeed peeling off after the first year of use, unless you keep it in a case (I did not) and use it with extreme caution (I did not).

I dropped it several times, it always kept going. Contacts on the most-frequently used keys are getting poor, I have to exert quite a bit of pressure to pick up or make a call.

I expect this unit to die before the end of its 3rd year of life. At $250, I owned it for about $7.50 a months. Based on my usage, next time I'll stick to the touch-screen, perhaps get a Skype-compatible (T-Mobile does not like to sell one), watch out for a good quality speakerphone, and make sure to get plenty of battery life. That is about $100 these days, but it can be less if I give up on using Skype on my home network on my cell phone.

I decided to give this a go as a budget Android phone. Our family is solidly in the iOS camp, but I had been curious about what Android had to offer. I brought this phone and got it hooked up through Verizon without any issues - I was in and out of the Verizon store in about 10 minutes (we already had a Verizon account with other devices on it).
